extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, patent attorneys/agents, patent office staff and IP lawyers operating under the Republic's Patents Act (national PCT phase and patent maintenance/licensing procedures)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements and procedural standards governing PCT national-phase entry, grant/sealing, duration, restoration, correction/amendment of specifications, joint ownership, and compulsory/licences of patents under the national Patents Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding of foreign search/report and service on patentee; compliance order
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of an application, the registrar shall forward a copy of the application (and prescribed particulars of any search report issued in another country for same subject-matter) to the patentee at the patentee’s address for service. If the patentee fails to comply with the application within three months of receipt of the copy at the patentee’s address for service, the applicant may apply to the commissioner for an order requiring compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the commissioner orders compliance and the order is not complied with, the commissioner may make further orders as deemed fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-defined terms apply in Chapter VA
rubrics_metrics.description: Any word or expression defined in the Patent Co-operation Treaty (PCT) shall have the same meaning as in that Treaty for purposes of the Chapter on international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act adopts PCT terminology and definitions to interpret Chapter VA provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: International application deemed national application when Republic designated
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application designating the Republic shall be deemed to be an application for a patent lodged at the patent office in terms of this Act, subject to the Chapter's provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deeming connects PCT filings to national procedures and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent office roles for PCT applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent office may act as receiving Office, designated Office, or elected Office for international (PCT) applications depending on circumstances (e.g., if lodged by a resident/national, if Republic is designated, or if applicant elects Republic for Chapter II examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different procedural duties and options apply depending on which role the national office occupies under the PCT filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on commencement of national phase processing (early commencement exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent office shall not commence processing the national phase of an international application before expiration of the period referred to in section 43E(1) unless the applicant complies with section 43E and lodges a written request for early commencement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early commencement requires compliance with national-phase entry requirements and a written request by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to commence national phase (payment, translation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before expiry of the applicable PCT period (Article 22 or 39) or further prescribed period, the applicant must: (a) pay the prescribed national fee to the patent office; and (b) if the international application was not lodged/published in English, lodge within the prescribed period a translation of the international application with prescribed contents in an official language of the Republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply within the period causes the international application, insofar as the Republic is designated/elected, to be deemed abandoned. The registrar may extend the period once for up to three months on application.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT instruments and national law precedence in national phase processing
rubrics_metrics.description: When processing the national phase the patent office shall apply the PCT, its regulations and administrative instructions, and other provisions of this Act; in event of conflict the PCT, its regulations and administrative instructions prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National processing is governed primarily by PCT instruments where they conflict with national provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific national adaptations for PCT national phase (agent, deemed complete specification, priority document rules, dates and publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various national modifications apply when processing a PCT national phase: section 9(b) does not apply; the applicant must be represented by an agent appointed within prescribed time; section 10 applies only on compliance with 43E; section 16(2) applies to PCT time limits; certain sections (e.g., 30(1),(5),(6), 32(5), 38, 43(3),(4)) are modified or do not apply; the description, claims, drawings and abstract in Article 3(2) of the PCT shall be deemed to be a complete specification; priority document requirements per Rule 17.1 and section 35(2) are addressed; the international filing date is the national filing date for national phase purposes; publication under Article 21 opens the national phase to public inspection once applicant complied with 43E; other mappings for corrections and amendments are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated mappings determine which national sections apply or are displaced for PCT-derived national-phase applications and how filing/priority/publication dates are treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of PCT Article 19 and 34 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made under Article 19 (corrections) that do not go beyond disclosure in the international application as filed, or amendments under Article 34 annexed to the international preliminary examination report, shall be deemed allowed under section 51 but may be set aside if they do not comply with national amendment restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such PCT amendments are generally accepted as allowed for national purposes but remain subject to national prohibition on new matter and other amendment limits and can be set aside under section 51(10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting and sealing of patent (timing and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as practicable after publication required by section 42, a patent in prescribed form shall be granted and sealed; sealing is deemed to have been effected on date of that publication. The patent has effect from the date of that publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealing/publication date establishes the effective date of the patent for rights purposes and procedural limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on instituting infringement proceedings post-sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: No proceedings for infringement may be instituted within nine months from the date of the sealing of the patent, except that the commissioner may, on good cause shown, grant leave to institute such proceedings at any time after sealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a provisional immunity period to permit resolution of issues (e.g., licensing) before litigation, subject to commissioner discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent (exclusive rights and purchaser rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: A granted patent confers on the patentee the right to exclude others from making, using, exercising, disposing of, offering to dispose of, or importing the invention for the duration of the patent. Disposal of a patented article by/for a patentee or licensee gives the purchaser the right to use, offer to dispose of and dispose of that article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope of monopoly and the rights conveyed to downstream purchasers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent duration and renewal fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent duration is 20 years from the date of application unless otherwise provided, subject to payment of prescribed renewal fees by patentee or agent. A patent lapses if renewal fee is not paid within the prescribed period; registrar may, on application and payment of additional fee, extend the period for payment for up to six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining patent rights requires timely payment of renewal fees; limited administrative relief is available for late payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of lapsed patent (grounds and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent lapsed due to non-payment of renewal fees, the patentee may apply in prescribed manner and on payment of prescribed fee to the registrar for restoration. If registrar is satisfied omission was unintentional and no undue delay occurred, registrar shall advertise the application and permit opposition; if no opposition registrar may restore or dismiss; if opposed, commissioner hears parties and decides; restoration is subject to payment of unpaid prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration requires establishing unintentional omission and prompt action; opposition and hearing rights exist for interested persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and limitations of restored patentees (actions and compensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee restored under section 47 may not institute proceedings or recover damages against persons who infringed after lapse during certain specified periods (e.g., six months after renewal due date until advertisement), persons who used/disposed/imported during that period, or persons who commenced using during that period and later continued — limited to those particular persons and their successors. Persons who expended money/time acting in good faith during the lapse may apply for compensation; the commissioner may assess compensation; assessed amounts are not recoverable as debt but unpaid compensation may cause the patent to lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects third parties who relied on lapse; creates remedial compensation route rather than full retroactive infringement exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership rights and restraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent is granted jointly, each joint patentee is entitled to equal undivided share absent agreement. In absence of agreement or consent of other joint patentees, a joint patentee is not entitled unilaterally to exploit, licence, assign, or take steps/proceedings relating to the patent (subject to limited exceptions such as paying renewal fees). Disposal by one joint patentee vests the acquirer with equal dealing rights. Any joint patentee may institute infringement proceedings but must notify others; other joint patentees may intervene; damages awarded to plaintiff are assessed as if sole patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects co-owners' interests and requires coordination or commissioner resolution for disputes; commissioner may order assignment/compensation and resolve disputes to preserve/exploit the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of clerical/translation errors and other amendments by registrar/commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrar or commissioner may authorize correction of clerical or translation errors in any patent/application/document or the register, and may authorize other amendments for which Act contains no express provision. Corrections may be made on written request with prescribed fee or without such request. If correction proposed otherwise than on request, registrar must give notice to patentee/applicant and others concerned and allow opportunity to be heard. If proposed correction would materially alter scope, registrar may require advertisement; opposition is possible and commissioner decides contested matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides administrative route for non-substantive corrections and a controlled process (notice/advertisement/opposition) where corrections may affect substantive scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to provisional and complete specifications (scope limits and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or patentee may apply to amend provisional or complete specification, setting out nature and full reasons. Applications open to public inspection must be advertised. Any person may oppose; commissioner/registrar determines whether and on what conditions amendment is allowed. Provisional specification amendments are allowed for corrections/obvious mistakes but must not introduce new matter or matter not in substance disclosed. No amendment of a complete specification that becomes open to public inspection after acceptance shall be allowed if it would introduce new matter or a claim not fairly based on pre-amendment disclosure, or include any claim not wholly within scope of a pre-existing claim. Supplementary disclosure may be allowed in narrow circumstances before acceptance published, but priority of new matter is the date of supplementary disclosure. Amendments during court proceedings must be made to the court; amendments violating section provisions may be set aside by commissioner or court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition on introducing new matter; public inspection/acceptance freezes allowable scope; opposition and judicial review routes preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of register
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrar may order rectification (making, amending, deleting entries) of the register either on request in prescribed manner or without such request; where intending to act without request, registrar must give notice to patentee/applicant and others who appear concerned and allow opportunity to be heard before making order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative correction of registry entries requires procedural fairness via notice/hearing where registrar initiates rectification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement 'licences of right' — prerequisites and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may apply post-sealing to have a patent endorsed 'licences of right'. The registrar shall endorse if satisfied the patentee is not precluded by contract from granting licences. After endorsement: any person is entitled to a licence as of right on conditions (if not agreed) to be decided by the commissioner; commissioner may replace pre-existing licences; no interdict (except for importation) in infringement proceedings if defendant undertakes to take a licence determined by commissioner; renewal fee payable after endorsement is halved; licensee may call on patentee to institute proceedings and may institute if patentee fails; endorsement must be recorded in register and advertised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorsement opens patents to compulsory licensing as of right with specified consequences for enforcement, renewal fee reduction, and administrative monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of 'licences of right' endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may apply for cancellation of endorsement. Registrar may cancel where balance of renewal fees payable if not endorsed is paid and registrar satisfied there is no existing licence or all licensees consent. Persons claiming preclusion by contract at endorsement may apply within prescribed period for cancellation; on cancellation patentee must pay balance of renewal fees or patent will lapse. Similar treatment applies for patents of addition. Cancellation restores rights/liabilities as if endorsement had not been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation requires clearing financial differences and resolving third-party contract claims; statutory safeguards for interested persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licences for dependent patents (conditions to grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where working of a dependent patent without infringement depends on obtaining a licence under a prior patent and agreement cannot be reached, proprietor of dependent patent may apply for licence; commissioner may grant a licence on conditions (including restriction to working dependent patent only). Commissioner shall not grant such a licence unless: (a) the dependent patent involves an important technical advance of considerable economic significance relative to the prior patent; (b) the proprietor of the dependent patent granted the proprietor of the prior patent on reasonable terms a cross-licence to use the dependent invention; and (c) the use authorised under the prior patent is not assignable except with assignment of the dependent patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects prior patent proprietor unless dependent patent demonstrates significant technical/economic advancement and reciprocal reasonable cross-licensing has been offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licences for abuse of patent rights (grounds and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person alleging abuse of patent rights may apply for a compulsory licence. Rights are deemed abused if (inter alia): the patented invention is not being worked in the Republic commercially or adequately after 4 years from application or 3 years from sealing (whichever later) with no satisfactory reason; demand in the Republic is not met adequately on reasonable terms; refusal to grant licences on reasonable terms prejudices trade/industry/agriculture or public interest; demand is met by importation and price charged is excessive relative to countries of manufacture. Patentee and interested parties may oppose. Commissioner considers merits and may order grant of licence on conditions (including prohibition on importation by licensee) or refuse. Licences under this section are non-exclusive and non-transferable except with business transfer. Commissioner must have regard to relevant facts (risks to licensee, R&D by patentee, usual licence terms). Commissioner may deem licence to have been granted as of the date application received, may amend or revoke licences, and shall act to avoid the abuse found. Licensee under such licence has same rights/obligations as other licensees. Commissioner may award costs and consider nature/extent of abuse and whether voluntary licence could have avoided application. 'Patented article' is broadly defined to include products of processes and machines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides public-interest and market-failure safety valve enabling compulsory licensing subject to proportionality, procedural fairness, and consideration of patentee's investments and licensing norms.
